newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Grand Union debt extends slide. [CORRECTED 10:10 GMT 31/5]
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Grand Union debt extends slide. [CORRECTED 10:10 GMT 31/5]

text.p: Junk bonds of Grand Union Copaging n continued to plummet on Friday amid otherwise light trading activity in the U.S. corporate bond market, traders said.

The company's $595 million in outstanding 12 percent senior notes dropped as low as 76 from their opening price of 84 on Friday. By the end of the day, bottom-fishing investors helped push the price up to 79.
Grand Union bonds dropped from the high eighties on Thursday after dissappointing earnings prompted two rating agencies to cut the supermarket operator's debt ratings.

In the broader high-yield market, prices of outstanding bonds continued to benefit from the paucity of new issues to be priced this week. Junk bonds ended the day 1/4 a point higher on modest trading activity, traders said.
But market sources said the strong market was not enough to help Paging Network do Brasil's $125 million eight-year note issue, the only junk deal to hit the market on Friday.

The offering from the Brazilian paging services company priced at the wide end of price talk to yield 13.50 (corrects from "13:25") percent. Bond investors were also given warrants to purchase up to seven percent of the company to sweeten the offer.
New issuance of investment grade debt was similarly subdued on Friday.
Washington Mutual Inc sold $400 million in 30-year capital securities to yield 8.392 percent via Lehman Brothers Inc.
BankBoston Corp sold $250 million in 30-year floating rate capital securities at 75 basis points over three-month Libor via Morgan Stanley & Co.
In secondary trading, investment-grade bonds finished a week of strong gains on a quiet note, remaining unchanged to Treasuries on the day.
Traders said numerous market participants had taken the day off in order to study for the sitting of the Chartered Financial Analyst exam which will be held tomorrow.
In other markets, the Dow Jones industrial average rose slightly less than one point to 7331.04.
But Treasuries rose for the second straight day on Friday, aided by heavy foreign buying.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 27/32 to 96-14/32, pushing its yield down to 6.91 percent.
